source.text: Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐγὼ Παῦλος παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς διὰ τῆς πραΰτητος καὶ ἐπιεικείας τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς κατὰ πρόσωπον μὲν ταπεινὸς ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀπὼν δὲ θαρρῶ εἰς ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Myself but I Paul appeal to you through the meekness and gentleness of the Christ, who according to face indeed [am] humble among you, being absent but am bold toward you;

en.L: Now I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, I who [am] humble when face to face among you, but when absent am bold toward you.
en.B: I, Paul, make this appeal to you myself, by the meekness and gentleness of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. I am the one who is humble when I am with you in person, but bold with you when I am at a distance.
en.R: I, Paul, am asking you this myself, and I ask it in the gentle, humble way that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} showed. Some people say that I am humble and weak when I am with you, but bold toward you when I am far away.

fr.L: Moi-même, Paul, je vous exhorte par la douceur et la bienveillance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, moi qui, face à face, [suis] humble parmi vous, mais qui, absent, suis hardi envers vous.
fr.B: Moi, Paul, je vous adresse moi-même cet appel, par la douceur et la bienveillance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. C’est moi qui suis humble quand je suis en personne avec vous, mais hardi envers vous quand je suis loin.
fr.R: Moi, Paul, je vous le demande moi-même, et je vous le demande avec la douceur et l’humilité que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a montrées. Certains disent que je suis humble et faible quand je suis avec vous, mais plein d’audace envers vous quand je suis loin.

es.L: Y yo mismo, Pablo, {{plural_you:los|os}} exhorto por la mansedumbre y la bondad del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, yo que, cara a cara, [soy] humilde entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero, ausente, soy audaz con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Yo, Pablo, {{plural_you:les|os}} hago personalmente este ruego, por la mansedumbre y la bondad {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Yo soy ese que es humilde cuando está con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en persona, pero atrevido con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando está lejos.
es.R: Yo, Pablo, {{plural_you:les|os}} pido esto personalmente, y lo hago con la manera amable y humilde que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} mostró. Algunos dicen que soy humilde y débil cuando estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero atrevido con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando estoy lejos.

sw.L: Basi mimi mwenyewe Paulo nawasihi kwa upole na wema wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, mimi ambaye ana kwa ana ni mnyenyekevu kati yenu, lakini nikiwa mbali ni shupavu kwenu.
sw.B: Mimi Paulo mwenyewe nawasihi, kwa upole na wema wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mimi ndiye ambaye ni mnyenyekevu ninapokuwa pamoja nanyi ana kwa ana, lakini shupavu kwenu ninapokuwa mbali.
sw.R: Mimi Paulo mwenyewe ninawaomba jambo hili, nami ninawaomba kwa upole na unyenyekevu kama ule ambao {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} alionyesha. Watu fulani husema kwamba mimi ni mnyonge na mpole ninapokuwa pamoja nanyi, lakini ni shupavu kwenu ninapokuwa mbali.

vi.L: Chính tôi, Phao-lô, nài khuyên anh chị em bởi sự nhu mì và hiền hòa của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, tôi là người khi đối mặt giữa anh chị em thì khiêm nhường, nhưng khi vắng mặt thì dạn dĩ đối với anh chị em.
vi.B: Chính tôi, Phao-lô, nài khuyên anh chị em, bởi sự nhu mì và hiền hòa của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Tôi là người khiêm nhường khi gặp mặt anh chị em, nhưng lại dạn dĩ với anh chị em khi ở xa.
vi.R: Chính tôi, Phao-lô, xin anh chị em điều này, và tôi xin với tấm lòng nhu mì, hiền hòa mà {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã bày tỏ. Có người nói rằng khi ở với anh chị em thì tôi khiêm nhường và yếu ớt, nhưng khi ở xa thì tôi lại dạn dĩ với anh chị em.

ko.L: 여러분과 얼굴을 마주하고 있을 때에는 여러분 가운데서 비천하고, 떠나 있을 때에는 여러분에게 담대한 나 바울은, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 온유함과 너그러움으로 친히 여러분에게 권합니다.
ko.B: 나 바울은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 온유함과 너그러움을 힘입어 직접 여러분에게 이렇게 권합니다. 나는 여러분과 함께 있을 때에는 비천하지만, 멀리 떨어져 있을 때에는 여러분에게 담대한 사람입니다.
ko.R: 나 바울이 직접 여러분에게 부탁합니다. 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 보여 주신 온유하고 겸손한 모습으로 이것을 부탁합니다. 어떤 사람들은 내가 여러분과 함께 있을 때에는 비굴하고 약하지만, 멀리 떨어져 있을 때에는 여러분에게 대담하다고 말합니다.

decisions.choice: chapters 10-13 form a distinct section of the letter, sharp in tone: Paul's defense of his work against rivals in Corinth
alternatives: a continuation in the same tone as chapters 1-9
decisions.reason: With this verse the tone of the letter changes sharply. After the warm confidence of chapter 7 (7:4, 16) and the appeal for the collection in chapters 8-9, Paul writes with irony, warning and self-defense to the end of chapter 13. The change is widely noticed, and some have taken chapters 10-13 to be part of another letter of Paul's to Corinth, later joined to chapters 1-9. Every manuscript of 2 Corinthians has these chapters here, after chapter 9, and the translation reads them where they stand.

decisions.choice: Paul speaks emphatically in his own name
decisions.reason: Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐγὼ Παῦλος ("I myself, Paul") is unusually emphatic. The letter came from Paul and Timothy (1:1) and often says "we", but the charges answered in these chapters are against Paul himself, and he answers them in person.

decisions.choice: the meekness and gentleness of Christ: his gentle, unassuming way and his kind forbearance, the ground and manner of Paul's appeal
alternatives: Paul's own meekness, as a follower of Christ
decisions.reason: πραΰτητος is gentleness that does not assert itself; ἐπιεικείας is kindness that does not insist on its rights. Jesus called himself gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29), using words from the same roots as πραΰτητος and ταπεινὸς. Paul appeals by Christ's character, and he will act toward the Corinthians in the same way if he can.

decisions.choice: appeal: to urge earnestly
decisions.reason: παρακαλῶ is the verb used for comfort in chapters 1 and 7 (1:4; 7:6), but here, with a request following in verse 2, it has its other common sense: to urge or plead with someone (as in 2:8; 5:20).

decisions.choice: who: Paul, not Christ; the words echo what his critics say of him
alternatives: a straightforward description Paul gives of himself
decisions.reason: ὃς goes back to "I myself, Paul", not to Christ. ταπεινὸς here has the bad sense of lowly or feeble, and κατὰ πρόσωπον means "in person". Verse 10 shows that some in Corinth said Paul was forceful in his letters but weak in person; Paul repeats the charge in order to answer it. Whether these are his critics' very words is uncertain. The irony is that the lowliness they despise belongs to Christ's own way (m3).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. The Greek has the article, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Some people say that I am humble and weak ...
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Paul is repeating what his critics say (m5, and verse 10), and adds "weak" to show that "humble" is meant as an insult here.

decisions.choice: du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, with the article outside the span (for chapters 10-11)
decisions.reason: French needs the article with the title after a preposition, at Literal too, so it stays outside the span and both options read naturally ("du Christ" / "du Messie"), as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: upole na wema
decisions.reason: "Upole" is meekness, a gentle, unassuming way; the second word is kind forbearance (meaning decision), said with "wema" (kindness). "Uvumilivu" is kept for endurance (6:4).

decisions.choice: shupavu
decisions.reason: "Shupavu" is firm and bold, ready to stand up to people, the sense here and in verse 2. "Ujasiri" is kept for open, plain speech (3:12), and "mkali" (harsh) would say more than the Greek.

decisions.choice: "sự nhu mì và hiền hòa" for prautes and epieikeia
decisions.reason: The gentle, unassuming way of Christ and his kind forbearance (m3). "Nhu mì" is the word the Vietnamese Galatians 5:23 and Colossians 3:12 use for prautes; "hiền hòa" gives the forbearing kindness of epieikeia, as in Philippians 4:5.

decisions.choice: "nài khuyên" (L, B); "xin" (R) for parakaleo
decisions.reason: To urge earnestly (m4); as in Romans 12:1 and 2 Corinthians 2:8.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" at every level for kauchaomai and kauchesis in chapters 10-12
decisions.reason: In chapters 10-13 Paul is forced into the rivals' kind of boasting and calls it folly (m1); "khoe mình" keeps the edge of the word, where "tự hào" would make it sound like proper pride. The boasting "in the Lord" of 10:17 uses the same word, so the contrast is visible.

decisions.choice: "온유함과 너그러움" (L, B); "온유하고 겸손한 모습" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the pair as gentleness that does not assert itself and kindness that does not insist on its rights.

decisions.choice: "비천하다" (L, B); "비굴하고 약하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word here in its bad sense, lowly or feeble, as Paul's critics say; "겸손" would praise him.

decisions.choice: Literal puts the relative clause about Paul before "나 바울은"
decisions.reason: Korean relative clauses come before the noun; so the clause can only go with Paul, as the meaning decision reads it, not with Christ.

decisions.choice: "권하다" (L, B); "부탁하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb here as urging, not comfort.

source.text: δέομαι δὲ τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι τῇ πεποιθήσει ᾗ λογίζομαι τολμῆσαι ἐπί τινας τοὺς λογιζομένους ἡμᾶς ὡς κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦντας.

records.literal_gloss: I beg but the not being present to be bold with the confidence with which I reckon to be daring against some, the [ones] reckoning us as according to flesh walking.

en.L: I beg [you] that when I am present I may not [have to] be bold with the confidence with which I reckon to be daring against some who reckon us as walking according to [the] flesh.
en.B: I beg you not to make me show boldness when I am with you, the confidence that I count on using against some people, those who count us as living by merely human standards.
en.R: Please do not make me be bold and harsh with you when I come. I expect that I will have to stand up boldly to some people there. They think that we live the way selfish people do.

fr.L: Je [vous] prie de ne pas [devoir], une fois présent, être hardi avec l’assurance avec laquelle j’estime oser [agir] contre certains qui estiment que nous marchons selon la chair.
fr.B: Je vous en prie : ne m’obligez pas, quand je serai là, à faire preuve de hardiesse, avec cette assurance que je compte bien employer contre certaines personnes, celles qui nous comptent parmi ceux qui vivent selon des critères purement humains.
fr.R: S’il vous plaît, ne me forcez pas à être hardi et dur avec vous quand je viendrai. Je pense que je devrai tenir tête avec audace à certaines personnes là-bas. Elles pensent que nous vivons comme vivent les gens égoïstes.

es.L: Y ruego que, estando presente, no [tenga que] ser audaz con la confianza con que considero atreverme contra algunos que nos consideran como si anduviéramos según [la] carne.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} ruego que no me {{plural_you:obliguen|obliguéis}} a mostrarme audaz cuando esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, con la firmeza con que cuento enfrentarme a algunos, a esos que nos cuentan entre los que viven con criterios meramente humanos.
es.R: Por favor, no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} que tenga que ser atrevido y duro con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando vaya. Creo que tendré que enfrentarme con valentía a algunas personas de allí. Ellas piensan que vivimos como vive la gente egoísta.

sw.L: Lakini naomba kwamba nikiwapo nisilazimike kuwa shupavu kwa uhakika ule ambao nadhani kuuthubutu juu ya baadhi ya watu wanaotudhania kuwa tunaenenda kwa kufuata mwili.
sw.B: Nawasihi msinilazimishe kuonyesha ushupavu nitakapokuwa pamoja nanyi, ule uhakika ambao nadhani nitautumia dhidi ya watu fulani, wale wanaotudhania kuwa tunaishi kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu tu.
sw.R: Tafadhali msinifanye niwe shupavu na mkali kwenu nitakapokuja. Natarajia kwamba nitalazimika kusimama imara dhidi ya watu fulani huko. Wao wanadhani kwamba tunaishi kama watu wenye ubinafsi.

vi.L: Tôi nài xin [anh chị em] để khi có mặt, tôi khỏi phải dạn dĩ với sự tin chắc mà tôi tính sẽ dùng để mạnh bạo chống lại một số người là những người tính rằng chúng tôi bước đi theo xác thịt.
vi.B: Tôi nài xin anh chị em đừng buộc tôi phải tỏ ra dạn dĩ khi tôi đến với anh chị em, tức là sự tin chắc mà tôi tính sẽ phải dùng để đối phó với một số người, là những người tính rằng chúng tôi sống theo tiêu chuẩn thuần túy con người.
vi.R: Xin anh chị em đừng để tôi phải nghiêm khắc và cứng rắn với anh chị em khi tôi đến. Tôi nghĩ rằng tôi sẽ phải dạn dĩ đối đầu với một số người ở đó. Họ cho rằng chúng tôi sống như những người ích kỷ.

ko.L: 내가 [여러분에게] 간구합니다. 내가 가서 있을 때에, 우리를 육신을 따라 행하는 사람처럼 여기는 어떤 사람들에게 대담하게 대하리라고 내가 여기는 그 확신으로 담대하게 [행하지] 않게 해 주십시오.
ko.B: 여러분에게 간청합니다. 내가 여러분과 함께 있을 때 담대하게 행동하지 않아도 되게 해 주십시오. 나는 우리를 사람의 기준으로만 사는 사람으로 여기는 어떤 사람들에게 그런 확신으로 맞서려고 생각하고 있습니다.
ko.R: 부디 내가 갈 때 여러분에게 대담하고 엄하게 대하지 않아도 되게 해 주십시오. 나는 그곳에서 어떤 사람들에게 대담하게 맞서야 할 것이라고 생각합니다. 그들은 우리가 자기만 생각하는 사람들처럼 산다고 여깁니다.

decisions.choice: Paul begs the church not to make it necessary for him to be severe when he comes
decisions.reason: δέομαι is a strong word for asking, "I beg". τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι means "that I may not, when present, be bold": he asks the Corinthians to put things right before he arrives, so that he need not use against them the boldness his critics say he has only in letters (verse 1). He is ready to use it against "some" (13:2, 10).

decisions.choice: reckon: to count on, and to count someone as something; Paul plays on the word
decisions.reason: The same verb comes twice: λογίζομαι ("I reckon, I count on") and λογιζομένους ("those who reckon, count us"). Paul counts on being bold against those who count him as a merely human operator. The verb comes back in verses 7 and 11. τολμῆσαι ("to dare, to be daring") returns in verse 12 and 11:21.

decisions.choice: walking according to the flesh: living by merely human standards and motives
alternatives: living in a body, as a weak human being
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a Jewish way of saying "live, conduct oneself". κατὰ σάρκα ("according to the flesh") is the charge Paul answered in 1:17: that he plans and acts as people do without God, out of self-interest. Verse 3 answers it.

decisions.choice: "us": Paul himself, perhaps with his companions
alternatives: Paul and all his fellow workers equally
decisions.reason: Paul moves from "I" to "us" within the sentence. As elsewhere in the letter (1:8), the plural mostly means Paul, since the charge is against him (verses 1, 10).

decisions.choice: living by merely human standards (B); live the way selfish people do (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:17 and 5:16, Literal keeps "flesh", while Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3). "Worldly" is avoided because it would blur the word with "world".

decisions.choice: count on ... count us
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps Paul's play on the one verb (m2) with an everyday English word.

decisions.choice: selon la chair (L); selon des critères purement humains (B); comme vivent les gens égoïstes (R), the same in 10:3 and 11:18
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "la chair" (style guide section 9); Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3), as the English does, and avoid "mondain", which would blur the word with "le monde".

decisions.choice: j’estime ... qui estiment (L); je compte ... qui nous comptent (B)
decisions.reason: Paul plays on one verb (m2); each level uses one French verb for both uses so that the play can be heard.

decisions.choice: cuento ... nos cuentan
decisions.reason: Paul plays on one verb, to count on and to count someone as something (meaning decision). Spanish "contar" has both senses, so Balanced keeps the play, as the English does with "count on ... count us"; Literal keeps "considerar" twice.

decisions.choice: según [la] carne (L); con criterios meramente humanos (B); como vive la gente egoísta (R)
alternatives: según la carne at every level
decisions.reason: As in 5:16: Literal keeps "carne" so the word can be traced through 10:2-4 and 11:18; Balanced says what it means here, merely human standards; Readable follows the English Readable.

decisions.choice: nadhani ... wanaotudhania
decisions.reason: Paul plays on one verb, to count on and to count someone as something (meaning decision). Swahili keeps the play with one verb, "kudhani"; "kuhesabu" is kept for God's reckoning (Romans 4; 2 Corinthians 5:19), as in 6:8.

decisions.choice: tunaenenda kwa kufuata mwili
decisions.reason: As in 5:16, Literal keeps the walking picture with "kuenenda" and the flesh word "mwili"; Balanced says what it means, merely human standards.

decisions.choice: "bước đi theo xác thịt" (L); "sống theo tiêu chuẩn thuần túy con người" (B); "sống như những người ích kỷ" (R)
decisions.reason: Living by merely human standards and motives (m3). Literal keeps "bước đi" and "xác thịt" as in Romans 8:4; Balanced uses the book's phrase "thuần túy con người" for kata sarka.

decisions.choice: "tính" twice for logizomai (L, B)
decisions.reason: Paul plays on the word: what he counts on doing, and how they count him (m2). Vietnamese "tính" covers both senses, so the play survives.

decisions.choice: "여기다" for both uses of the verb (L)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that Paul plays on the word; Literal keeps one Korean verb so the play can be heard.

decisions.choice: "육신을 따라 행하는" (L); "사람의 기준으로만 사는" (B); "자기만 생각하는 사람들처럼 산다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as living by merely human standards; "행하다" is the project's Literal word for "walk" as a way of life, and "육신" its word for the flesh.

source.text: ἐν σαρκὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦντες οὐ κατὰ σάρκα στρατευόμεθα τὰ γὰρ ὅπλα τῆς στρατείας ἡμῶν οὐ σαρκικὰ ἀλλὰ δυνατὰ τῷ θεῷ πρὸς καθαίρεσιν ὀχυρωμάτων λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντες πᾶν νόημα εἰς τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες ἐκδικῆσαι πᾶσαν παρακοήν, ὅταν πληρωθῇ ὑμῶν ἡ ὑπακοή.

records.literal_gloss: In flesh for walking not according to flesh do we wage war, \v 4 for the weapons of the warfare of us [are] not fleshly but powerful to the God for demolition of strongholds, arguments demolishing \v 5 and every high thing lifting itself up against the knowledge of the God, and taking captive every thought into the obedience of the Christ, \v 6 and in readiness having to punish every disobedience, whenever may be fulfilled of you the obedience.

en.L: For though walking in [the] flesh, we do not wage war according to [the] flesh, \v 4 for the weapons of our warfare [are] not fleshly but powerful to God for [the] tearing down of strongholds, [as we are] tearing down arguments \v 5 and every high thing lifting itself up against the knowledge of God, and taking captive every thought into the obedience of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 6 and holding ourselves in readiness to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is made full.
en.B: We do live as human beings, but we do not fight our battles by merely human standards. \v 4 Our weapons in this fight are not merely human; they have power from God to tear down strongholds, and so we tear down arguments \v 5 and every proud tower raised against the knowledge of God. We capture every thought and lead it away to obey {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 6 We are prepared to punish all disobedience, once you yourselves have fully obeyed.
en.R: We are human, but we do not fight our battles the way humans usually do. \v 4 Our weapons are not human weapons. They have God's power, and they can knock down strong forts. We knock down clever arguments \v 5 and every proud wall that people build to keep themselves from knowing God. We capture every thought, like a prisoner of war, and make it obey {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 6 And once you have fully obeyed, we are ready to punish anyone who still disobeys.

fr.L: Car, bien que marchant dans la chair, nous ne faisons pas la guerre selon la chair, \v 4 car les armes de notre combat [ne sont] pas charnelles, mais puissantes pour Dieu pour la démolition des forteresses ; [nous] démolissons les raisonnements \v 5 et toute hauteur qui s’élève contre la connaissance de Dieu, et nous faisons prisonnière toute pensée pour l’obéissance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 6 et nous nous tenons prêts à punir toute désobéissance, quand votre obéissance sera complète.
fr.B: Nous vivons certes comme des êtres humains, mais nous ne menons pas notre combat selon des critères purement humains. \v 4 Les armes de notre combat ne sont pas purement humaines ; elles ont, par Dieu, la puissance d’abattre des forteresses. Ainsi nous abattons les raisonnements \v 5 et toute tour orgueilleuse dressée contre la connaissance de Dieu. Nous capturons toute pensée et l’emmenons captive pour qu’elle obéisse au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 6 Nous sommes prêts à punir toute désobéissance, une fois que vous-mêmes aurez pleinement obéi.
fr.R: Nous sommes des humains, mais nous ne menons pas nos combats comme les humains le font d’habitude. \v 4 Nos armes ne sont pas des armes humaines. Elles ont la puissance de Dieu, et elles peuvent renverser des forteresses. Nous renversons les raisonnements trop habiles \v 5 et chaque mur d’orgueil que les gens construisent pour ne pas connaître Dieu. Nous capturons chaque pensée, comme un prisonnier de guerre, et nous la faisons obéir au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 6 Et une fois que vous aurez complètement obéi, nous serons prêts à punir ceux qui désobéissent encore.

es.L: Porque, aunque andamos en [la] carne, no hacemos la guerra según [la] carne, \v 4 porque las armas de nuestra milicia no [son] carnales, sino poderosas para Dios para [la] destrucción de fortalezas, [mientras] destruimos argumentos \v 5 y toda altivez que se levanta contra el conocimiento de Dios, y llevamos cautivo todo pensamiento a la obediencia del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, \v 6 y estamos dispuestos a castigar toda desobediencia, cuando {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} obediencia sea completa.
es.B: Es verdad que vivimos como seres humanos, pero no libramos nuestras batallas con criterios meramente humanos. \v 4 Las armas con que luchamos no son meramente humanas; tienen poder de Dios para derribar fortalezas, y así derribamos argumentos \v 5 y toda torre orgullosa que se levanta contra el conocimiento de Dios. Capturamos todo pensamiento y lo llevamos a obedecer {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. \v 6 Estamos preparados para castigar toda desobediencia, una vez que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} obedecido del todo.
es.R: Somos humanos, pero no luchamos como suele luchar la gente. \v 4 Nuestras armas no son armas humanas. Tienen el poder de Dios y pueden derribar fortalezas. Derribamos argumentos astutos \v 5 y todo muro orgulloso que la gente levanta para no conocer a Dios. Capturamos cada pensamiento, como a un prisionero de guerra, y lo hacemos obedecer {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. \v 6 Y cuando {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} obedecido del todo, estaremos listos para castigar a cualquiera que siga desobedeciendo.

sw.L: Kwa maana tukienenda katika mwili, hatupigani vita kwa kufuata mwili, \v 4 kwa maana silaha za vita vyetu si za kimwili, bali zina nguvu kwa Mungu kwa kubomoa ngome, [tukiwa] tunabomoa hoja \v 5 na kila kilicho juu kinachojiinua dhidi ya ujuzi wa Mungu, na tukiteka kila wazo [kulileta] katika utii wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 6 na tukiwa tayari kuadhibu kila kutotii, utii wenu utakapotimizwa.
sw.B: Ni kweli tunaishi kama wanadamu, lakini hatupigani vita vyetu kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu tu. \v 4 Silaha zetu katika vita hivi si za kibinadamu tu; zina nguvu kutoka kwa Mungu za kubomoa ngome. Kwa hiyo tunabomoa hoja \v 5 na kila mnara wa kiburi uliojengwa dhidi ya kumjua Mungu. Tunateka kila wazo na kulipeleka litii {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 6 Tuko tayari kuadhibu kila kutotii, mara mtakapokuwa mmetii kikamilifu ninyi wenyewe.
sw.R: Sisi ni wanadamu, lakini hatupigani vita vyetu kwa jinsi wanadamu wanavyofanya kwa kawaida. \v 4 Silaha zetu si silaha za kibinadamu. Zina nguvu ya Mungu, nazo zinaweza kuangusha ngome imara. Tunaangusha hoja za werevu \v 5 na kila ukuta wa kiburi ambao watu hujenga ili wasimjue Mungu. Tunateka kila wazo, kama mfungwa wa vita, na kulifanya limtii {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 6 Na mtakapokuwa mmetii kikamilifu, tuko tayari kumwadhibu yeyote ambaye bado haitii.

vi.L: Vì dù bước đi trong xác thịt, chúng tôi không chiến đấu theo xác thịt; \v 4 vì khí giới của cuộc chiến đấu chúng tôi không thuộc xác thịt, nhưng có quyền năng đối với Đức Chúa Trời để phá đổ các đồn lũy, [khi chúng tôi] phá đổ các lý luận \v 5 và mọi điều cao ngạo dấy lên chống lại sự hiểu biết Đức Chúa Trời, và bắt mọi tư tưởng làm phu tù để vâng phục {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, \v 6 và sẵn sàng trừng phạt mọi sự không vâng phục, khi sự vâng phục của anh chị em được trọn vẹn.
vi.B: Chúng tôi vẫn sống như mọi con người, nhưng chúng tôi không chiến đấu theo tiêu chuẩn thuần túy con người. \v 4 Khí giới chúng tôi dùng trong cuộc chiến này không phải thuần túy của con người; chúng có quyền năng từ Đức Chúa Trời để phá đổ các đồn lũy. Vì vậy chúng tôi phá đổ các lý luận \v 5 và mọi tháp cao ngạo dựng lên chống lại sự hiểu biết Đức Chúa Trời. Chúng tôi bắt mọi tư tưởng làm phu tù và dẫn đi để vâng phục {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. \v 6 Chúng tôi sẵn sàng trừng phạt mọi sự không vâng phục, một khi chính anh chị em đã hoàn toàn vâng phục.
vi.R: Chúng tôi là con người, nhưng chúng tôi không chiến đấu theo cách con người thường làm. \v 4 Khí giới của chúng tôi không phải là khí giới của con người. Chúng có quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời, và có thể đánh sập những đồn lũy kiên cố. Chúng tôi đánh sập những lý lẽ khôn khéo \v 5 và mọi bức tường kiêu ngạo mà người ta dựng lên để khỏi phải biết Đức Chúa Trời. Chúng tôi bắt giữ mọi ý nghĩ, như bắt tù binh, và buộc nó vâng phục {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. \v 6 Và một khi anh chị em đã hoàn toàn vâng phục, chúng tôi sẵn sàng trừng phạt bất cứ ai còn bất tuân.

ko.L: 우리가 육신 안에서 살고 있지만, 육신을 따라 싸우지는 않습니다. \v 4 우리 싸움의 무기는 육신의 것이 아니라 하나님께 능력 있는 것이어서, 요새들을 무너뜨립니다. 우리는 이론들을 무너뜨리고 \v 5 하나님을 아는 지식을 거슬러 일어나는 모든 높은 것을 [무너뜨리며], 모든 생각을 사로잡아 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 순종하게 하고, \v 6 여러분의 순종이 온전하게 될 때에는 모든 불순종을 벌할 준비가 되어 있습니다.
ko.B: 우리는 사람으로서 살고 있지만, 사람의 기준으로만 싸우지는 않습니다. \v 4 우리가 이 싸움에서 쓰는 무기는 사람의 무기가 아닙니다. 그 무기에는 요새를 무너뜨리는 하나님의 능력이 있습니다. 그래서 우리는 이론들을 무너뜨리고, \v 5 하나님을 아는 지식을 거슬러 세운 모든 교만한 탑을 무너뜨립니다. 우리는 모든 생각을 사로잡아 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 순종하도록 이끌어 갑니다. \v 6 그리고 여러분 자신이 온전히 순종하게 되면, 우리는 모든 불순종을 벌할 준비가 되어 있습니다.
ko.R: 우리는 사람이지만, 사람들이 흔히 싸우는 방식으로 싸우지 않습니다. \v 4 우리의 무기는 사람이 만든 무기가 아닙니다. 그 무기에는 하나님의 능력이 있어서 튼튼한 요새를 허물 수 있습니다. 우리는 그럴듯한 주장들을 허뭅니다. \v 5 그리고 사람들이 하나님을 알지 못하게 하려고 쌓은 모든 교만한 성벽을 허뭅니다. 우리는 전쟁에서 포로를 사로잡듯이 모든 생각을 사로잡아 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 순종하게 합니다. \v 6 그리고 여러분이 온전히 순종하게 되면, 우리는 그래도 여전히 순종하지 않는 사람이 있다면 누구든지 벌할 준비가 되어 있습니다.

decisions.choice: in the flesh: in ordinary, weak human life; according to the flesh, fleshly: by merely human standards and means
alternatives: both phrases in the same, bad sense
decisions.reason: Paul answers the charge of verse 2 with a play on words. ἐν σαρκὶ ("in flesh") is simply being human, as in Galatians 2:20; κατὰ σάρκα ("according to flesh") and σαρκικὰ ("fleshly") mean working by human standards, without God. He is human, but his methods are not merely human.

decisions.choice: a picture of siege warfare: fortresses torn down, towers brought low, prisoners led away
decisions.reason: στρατευόμεθα means to serve as a soldier or wage a campaign. ὀχυρωμάτων were fortresses; ὕψωμα is anything raised high, such as a tower or rampart; αἰχμαλωτίζοντες means to take prisoner in war. The picture is of an army that pulls down a city's defenses and leads its people away captive. Paul uses the same kind of picture for God's weapons in 6:7 and Ephesians 6:11-17.

decisions.choice: tearing down strongholds may echo Proverbs 21:22
decisions.reason: The Greek of Proverbs 21:22 uses the same noun, ὀχύρωμα, for the stronghold of the ungodly that a wise man pulls down. In Paul's picture the strongholds are arguments and proud thoughts (verse 5), not places.

decisions.choice: powerful to God: made powerful by God, mighty in his service
decisions.reason: The dative τῷ θεῷ can mean "by God" (the power comes from him), "for God" (in his cause), or, as a Hebrew-style intensive, "mighty before God", that is, very mighty (compare the Greek of Jonah 3:3, "a city great to God"). In each reading the weapons' power is not human; "by God" fits the contrast with "fleshly" best.

decisions.choice: arguments: reasoned objections; every high thing: every proud barrier against knowing God
decisions.reason: λογισμοὺς are reasonings, calculations or arguments: here the clever case made against Paul and his gospel, and the kind of reasoning prized in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:19-20; 3:20). "The knowledge of God" is knowing God, which the gospel brings (2:14; 4:6); every proud argument raised against it is a tower to be brought down.

decisions.choice: every thought taken captive into obedience to Christ
alternatives: every thought of Paul's own only
decisions.reason: νόημα is a thought, plan or scheme (2:11; 4:4; 11:3). τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ is the obedience owed to Christ: the captured thoughts are made to serve him. The picture continues the war: prisoners led away under a new master.

decisions.choice: Paul will punish the disobedience of those who still resist, once the church as a whole has returned to obedience
alternatives: the Corinthians' own disobedience in general
decisions.reason: ἐκδικῆσαι means to punish or see justice done, not personal revenge. "Your obedience" is the church's (2:9; 7:15); "every disobedience" is then what remains among those who still oppose Paul (13:2). The participles of verses 4-6 are loosely joined to "we wage war" in verse 3, as Paul's long sentences often are.

decisions.choice: live as human beings ... by merely human standards ... not merely human (B); human ... the way humans usually do ... not human weapons (R)
alternatives: in the flesh ... according to the flesh ... fleshly
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh" so the wordplay can be traced; Balanced and Readable give the sense of each phrase (m1), as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: tearing down ... tearing down (L); tear down ... tear down (B); knock down ... knock down (R)
decisions.reason: The noun and the participle come from one verb, which returns in verse 8 ("not for tearing you down"); each level keeps one English verb for all three.

decisions.choice: every proud wall that people build to keep themselves from knowing God; like a prisoner of war; anyone who still disobeys
alternatives: every high thing raised against the knowledge of God
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture and says whose disobedience is punished (m5, m6, m7).

decisions.choice: the long sentence broken into four (B) or six (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 3-6 are one Greek sentence; Balanced and Readable break it where each clause can stand, keeping its order. Readable puts the time clause of verse 6 first.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. The Greek has the article, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: la démolition, démolir (L); abattre (B); renverser (R), the same in verse 8
decisions.reason: The noun and the participle come from one verb, which returns in verse 8 ("not for tearing you down"); each level keeps one French verb for all three uses, as the English does.

decisions.choice: las armas de nuestra milicia
decisions.reason: The Greek has the verb "wage war" and then the noun for a military campaign; "milicia" keeps a second military word beside "hacer la guerra" without repeating it.

decisions.choice: kubomoa ... kubomoa (L, B); kuangusha ... kuangusha (R); ngome
decisions.reason: "Kubomoa" is to pull down a building or wall, the siege picture (meaning decision), and the same verb is used for both places, as in verse 8; Readable says "kuangusha" (knock down). "Ngome" is a fortress.

decisions.choice: kutotii
decisions.reason: "Kutotii" (not obeying) is the plain opposite of "utii" (obedience) in the same verse; "uasi" is kept for lawlessness (Romans 6:19; 2 Corinthians 6:14).

decisions.choice: "khí giới", "đồn lũy", "bắt ... làm phu tù" (L, B); "khí giới", "đồn lũy kiên cố", "bắt tù binh" (R)
decisions.reason: The picture of siege warfare (m2): weapons, fortresses torn down, prisoners led away. "Khí giới" is the word of the Vietnamese Romans 13:12 and Ephesians 6:11-13.

decisions.choice: "trong xác thịt ... theo xác thịt ... thuộc xác thịt" (L); "như mọi con người ... thuần túy con người" (B); "con người ... của con người" (R)
decisions.reason: Ordinary human life, and merely human standards and means (m1). Literal keeps the one word so the play on sarx can be traced; the other levels say what each use means.

decisions.choice: "có quyền năng đối với Đức Chúa Trời" (L), with "từ Đức Chúa Trời" (B) and "của Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
alternatives: "mạnh mẽ trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The dative is unclear: made powerful by God, or mighty in his service (m4, uncertain). Literal keeps the bare dative; Balanced and Readable take the more likely sense.

decisions.choice: "phá đổ ... phá đổ" (L, B); "đánh sập ... đánh sập" (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb twice, as in the English, for the fortresses and the arguments.

decisions.choice: "육신 안에서 ... 육신을 따라 ... 육신의 것" (L); "사람으로서 ... 사람의 기준으로만 ... 사람의 무기" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the first phrase as ordinary human life and the other two as merely human standards and means; Literal keeps one word so Paul's play on it can be heard.

decisions.choice: "요새", "높은 것", "사로잡다" (L); "요새", "교만한 탑", "사로잡다" (B); "요새", "교만한 성벽", "포로를 사로잡듯이" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the passage as a picture of siege warfare.

decisions.choice: "하나님께 능력 있는 것" (L); "하나님의 능력이 있다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves open whether the power comes from God or is used for him; Literal keeps the Greek's "to God" with "께", and the other levels follow the English.

decisions.choice: "이론" (L, B); "그럴듯한 주장" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as reasoned objections; "생각" is kept for the different word in verse 5.

records.literal_gloss: The [things] according to face you look at.

en.L: Look at the things before [your] face.
en.B: Look at what is right in front of you.
en.R: Look at the facts that are right in front of your eyes.

fr.L: Regardez ce qui est devant [votre] face.
fr.B: Regardez ce qui est sous vos yeux.
fr.R: Regardez les faits qui sont juste devant vos yeux.

es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} los hechos que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} delante de los ojos.

sw.L: Angalieni mambo yaliyo mbele ya uso [wenu].
sw.B: Angalieni yaliyo mbele ya macho yenu.
sw.R: Angalieni ukweli ulio wazi mbele ya macho yenu.

vi.L: Hãy nhìn những điều ở trước mặt [anh chị em].
vi.B: Hãy nhìn những gì ở ngay trước mắt anh chị em.
vi.R: Hãy nhìn vào những sự thật ở ngay trước mắt anh chị em.

ko.B: 여러분 바로 앞에 있는 것을 보십시오.
ko.R: 여러분의 눈앞에 있는 분명한 사실들을 보십시오.

decisions.choice: a command: look at what is plain to see
alternatives: a statement: you look at things only as they appear on the outside
a question: are you looking at outward appearances?
decisions.reason: βλέπετε can be read as a command or as a statement, since the forms are the same; the SBLGNT ends the sentence with a full stop, not a question mark, though a question is grammatically possible. Paul often uses this verb as a command (1 Corinthians 8:9; 10:12; 16:10; Philippians 3:2), and the next sentence goes on to point out a plain fact: Paul belongs to Christ as much as anyone. Read as a statement, the words are a rebuke: the Corinthians judge by outward show, as in 5:12 and 10:10. Both readings fit the passage.

decisions.choice: the things before your face: what is evident, in plain view
alternatives: outward appearances, as against what is within
decisions.reason: κατὰ πρόσωπον is the phrase of verse 1, "face to face". As a command, it points to facts the Corinthians can see for themselves, such as Paul's work among them (3:2-3). As a statement, it would mean appearances, as "in the face" does in 5:12.

decisions.choice: the facts
decisions.reason: Readable names what is in plain view (m2).

decisions.choice: ante [sus] ojos
decisions.reason: The Greek says "before the face"; Spanish says what is plain to see with "ante los ojos", and "rostro" with "sus" could be read as someone else's face.

decisions.choice: a command: "Hãy nhìn"
alternatives: "Anh chị em chỉ nhìn bề ngoài"
decisions.reason: The verb can be a statement or a command; the meaning decision takes it as a command (m1, uncertain), and so does the Vietnamese.

decisions.choice: A command, "보십시오", at every level
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision's reading of the verb as a command, with the SBLGNT's full stop.

source.text: εἴ τις πέποιθεν ἑαυτῷ Χριστοῦ εἶναι, τοῦτο λογιζέσθω πάλιν ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ὅτι καθὼς αὐτὸς Χριστοῦ οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone is confident in himself of Christ to be, this let him reckon again within himself, that just as he [is] of Christ, so also we.

en.L: If anyone is confident in {{gender:themselves|himself}} that {{gender:they are|he is}} of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, let {{gender:them|him}} reckon this again within {{gender:themselves|himself}}: that just as {{gender:they are|he is}} of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, so also [are] we.
en.B: Anyone who is confident of belonging to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} should think again and consider this: just as that person belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so do we.
en.R: Some people are sure that they belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. They should stop and think again. If they belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, then so do we.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un est persuadé en lui-même d’être du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, qu’il considère encore ceci en lui-même : de même qu’il est du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, ainsi aussi [le sommes]-nous.
fr.B: Celui qui est sûr d’appartenir au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} doit réfléchir encore et considérer ceci : tout comme lui appartient au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, nous aussi.
fr.R: Certaines personnes sont sûres d’appartenir au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Elles devraient s’arrêter et réfléchir encore. Si elles appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, alors nous aussi.

es.L: Si alguien confía en sí de ser {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, que considere esto otra vez dentro de sí: que así como esa persona [es] {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, así también nosotros.
es.B: Si alguien está seguro de pertenecer {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, que lo piense de nuevo y tenga en cuenta esto: así como esa persona pertenece {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, también nosotros.
es.R: Hay quienes están seguros de que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Deberían detenerse a pensarlo otra vez. Si ellos pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, nosotros también.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu ana uhakika ndani yake kwamba ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, alitafakari tena hili ndani yake: kwamba jinsi yeye alivyo wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, hivyo hivyo [tulivyo] sisi pia.

vi.L: Nếu ai tin chắc nơi chính mình rằng mình thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, thì người ấy hãy tự xét lại điều này: như người ấy thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thể nào, thì chúng tôi cũng [vậy].

decisions.choice: to be of Christ: to belong to Christ, as his servant
alternatives: to belong to a party that claims Christ's name (1 Corinthians 1:12)
decisions.reason: Χριστοῦ εἶναι ("to be of Christ") means belonging to him. Paul's rivals claimed a special standing as Christ's servants (11:23). The words recall the slogan "I am of Christ" in 1 Corinthians 1:12, but nothing here shows that the same group is meant.

decisions.choice: Paul does not deny the claim but sets his own beside it
decisions.reason: λογιζέσθω is the verb "reckon" of verse 2, now as a command in the third person: let such a person count again. Paul grants for the moment that his rival belongs to Christ and asks only that the same be granted to him. Later he goes further (11:13-15).

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:they are|he is}}; {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: τις ("anyone") is general, so the default pronouns are inclusive. Balanced says "that person" and Readable uses the plural, which need no setting.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un ... lui-même ... il", "celui qui ... lui", with no gender span (L, B)
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs gender spans for its pronouns. In French "quelqu’un" and "celui qui" already mean anyone, and the pronouns that refer back to them are ordinary generic French, so no span is used (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: alguien ... en sí ... dentro de sí ... esa persona, with no gender setting
alternatives: gender settings as in the English
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs gender settings for its pronouns; Spanish "alguien", "sí" and "esa persona" already include women and men, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: mtu, yeye, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Mtu" is a person of either sex and "yeye" is he or she alike, so the English gender spans have nothing to change in Swahili.

decisions.choice: "mình", "người ấy", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "mình" and "người ấy" are already man or woman.

decisions.choice: "thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" for "to be of Christ"
decisions.reason: To belong to Christ as his servant (m1); as in 1 Corinthians 3:23 and 15:23.

decisions.choice: "누구든지 ... 자기 ... 그는" (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "누구든지" and "자기" include women and men; the English Literal's gender spans have no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: "여겨야 합니다" (L)
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 2 and verse 11, kept in Literal.

decisions.choice: "... 께 속하다" for belonging to Christ, at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as belonging to Christ, as his servant.

source.text: ἐάν τε γὰρ περισσότερόν τι καυχήσωμαι περὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἡμῶν, ἧς ἔδωκεν ὁ κύριος εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν ὑμῶν, οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι, ἵνα μὴ δόξω ὡς ἂν ἐκφοβεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ τῶν ἐπιστολῶν·

records.literal_gloss: If even for more abundantly something I should boast about the authority of us, which gave the Lord for building up and not for tearing down of you, not I will be put to shame, \v 9 so that not I may seem as if to frighten you through the letters;

en.L: For even if I boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Lord gave for building [you] up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame, \v 9 so that I may not seem as though [I were] frightening you through [my] letters.
en.B: Suppose I boast rather more than I should about our authority, which the Lord gave us to build you up and not to tear you down: I will not be put to shame. \v 9 I would not want it to look as though I were out to terrify you by letter.
en.R: Even if I boast a bit too much about the authority we have from the Lord, that boasting will not put me to shame. The Lord gave us this authority to build you up, not to knock you down. \v 9 I do not want you to think I am just trying to scare you with my letters.

fr.L: Car même si je me vante un peu plus de notre autorité, que le Seigneur [nous] a donnée pour [votre] édification et non pour votre démolition, je ne serai pas couvert de honte, \v 9 afin que je ne paraisse pas comme [si je voulais] vous effrayer par [mes] lettres.
fr.B: Supposons que je me vante un peu trop de notre autorité, que le Seigneur nous a donnée pour vous édifier et non pour vous abattre : je ne serai pas couvert de honte. \v 9 Je ne voudrais pas avoir l’air de chercher à vous terroriser par mes lettres.
fr.R: Même si je me vante un peu trop de l’autorité que nous avons reçue du Seigneur, cette vantardise ne me couvrira pas de honte. Le Seigneur nous a donné cette autorité pour vous faire grandir, et non pour vous renverser. \v 9 Je ne veux pas que vous pensiez que j’essaie seulement de vous faire peur avec mes lettres.

es.L: Porque aunque me gloríe algo más de nuestra autoridad, que el Señor [nos] dio para edificación y no para destrucción de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no seré avergonzado, \v 9 para que no parezca como si quisiera {{plural_you:asustarlos|asustaros}} por medio de [mis] cartas.
es.B: Supongamos que me glorío algo más de la cuenta de nuestra autoridad, la que el Señor nos dio para {{plural_you:edificarlos|edificaros}} y no para {{plural_you:destruirlos|destruiros}}: no quedaré avergonzado. \v 9 No quiero dar la impresión de que intento {{plural_you:aterrorizarlos|aterrorizaros}} con mis cartas.
es.R: Aunque me gloríe un poco de más de la autoridad que tenemos del Señor, no tendré de qué avergonzarme. El Señor nos dio esta autoridad para {{plural_you:fortalecerlos|fortaleceros}}, no para {{plural_you:derribarlos|derribaros}}. \v 9 No quiero que {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que solo trato de {{plural_you:asustarlos|asustaros}} con mis cartas.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata nikijivunia kwa kiasi fulani zaidi kuhusu mamlaka yetu, ambayo Bwana alitupa kwa kuwajenga na si kwa kuwabomoa, sitaaibika, \v 9 ili nisionekane kana kwamba ninawatisha kupitia barua [zangu].
sw.B: Tuseme ninajivunia kupita kiasi kuhusu mamlaka yetu, ambayo Bwana alitupa ili tuwajenge na si ili tuwabomoe: sitaaibishwa. \v 9 Sipendi ionekane kana kwamba nataka kuwatisha kwa barua zangu.
sw.R: Hata nikijivunia kidogo kupita kiasi kuhusu mamlaka tuliyopewa na Bwana, kujivunia huko hakutaniaibisha. Bwana alitupa mamlaka haya ili tuwajenge, si ili tuwaangushe. \v 9 Sitaki mdhani kwamba ninajaribu tu kuwatisha kwa barua zangu.

vi.L: Vì dù tôi có khoe mình hơi nhiều hơn về quyền của chúng tôi, là quyền Chúa đã ban để gây dựng chứ không phải để phá đổ anh chị em, thì tôi cũng sẽ không bị hổ thẹn, \v 9 để tôi không có vẻ như muốn làm anh chị em sợ hãi bằng các thư.
vi.B: Giả sử tôi có khoe mình hơi quá về quyền của chúng tôi, là quyền Chúa ban cho chúng tôi để gây dựng anh chị em chứ không phải để phá đổ anh chị em, thì tôi cũng sẽ không bị hổ thẹn. \v 9 Tôi không muốn mình có vẻ như đang dùng thư từ để làm anh chị em khiếp sợ.
vi.R: Dù tôi có khoe mình hơi quá về quyền mà Chúa đã ban cho chúng tôi, thì sự khoe mình ấy cũng sẽ không làm tôi phải xấu hổ. Chúa ban cho chúng tôi quyền này để gây dựng anh chị em, chứ không phải để đánh đổ anh chị em. \v 9 Tôi không muốn anh chị em nghĩ rằng tôi chỉ tìm cách dọa anh chị em bằng những lá thư của tôi.

ko.L: 주님께서 여러분을 무너뜨리라고가 아니라 세우라고 우리에게 주신 우리의 권위에 대해 내가 조금 더 자랑한다 하더라도, 나는 부끄러움을 당하지 않을 것입니다. \v 9 내가 편지로 여러분을 위협하는 것처럼 보이지 않으려고 [이렇게 말합니다].
ko.B: 주님께서 여러분을 무너뜨리라고가 아니라 세우라고 우리에게 주신 권위에 대해 내가 지나치다 싶을 만큼 자랑한다고 합시다. 그래도 나는 부끄러움을 당하지 않을 것입니다. \v 9 나는 내가 편지로 여러분을 겁주려 한다고 보이고 싶지 않습니다.
ko.R: 내가 주님께 받은 권위에 대해 조금 지나치게 자랑하더라도, 그 자랑 때문에 내가 부끄러움을 당하지는 않을 것입니다. 주님께서 우리에게 이 권위를 주신 것은 여러분을 세우라고 주신 것이지 쓰러뜨리라고 주신 것이 아닙니다. \v 9 나는 여러분이 내가 편지로 여러분을 겁주려고만 한다고 생각하지 않기를 바랍니다.

decisions.choice: to boast: to speak with pride of one's standing; here Paul begins the boasting his rivals have forced on him
alternatives: proper pride in God's work only
decisions.reason: καυχήσωμαι begins the run of words for boasting that carries chapters 10-12 (10:13-17; 11:16-18, 30; 12:1, 5-6, 9). Paul's rivals boast of themselves; Paul is drawn into boasting too, but he boasts of the authority the Lord gave him and, later, of his weaknesses (11:30; 12:9). περισσότερόν τι ("somewhat more") grants that it may seem excessive.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and power of an apostle, given by the Lord for building the church up
decisions.reason: ἐξουσίας is the authority of an apostle, given by "the Lord", here Christ, who sent him (1:1). Paul says the same in nearly the same words in 13:10. καθαίρεσιν picks up the "tearing down" of strongholds in verse 4: Paul's power tears down proud arguments, but it was given to build up the church, not to tear it down.

decisions.choice: building up and tearing down: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: God appointed Jeremiah to tear down and to build (Jeremiah 1:10; 24:6). Paul describes his own commission in the same terms, with the stress on building.

decisions.choice: I will not be put to shame: his boast will prove true; and so his letters are not empty threats
alternatives: "so that" goes with an unspoken "I say this"
decisions.reason: αἰσχυνθήσομαι means his boast will not be shown up as empty. Verse 9 begins with ἵνα ("so that"), with no main verb close at hand. It may go with "I will not be put to shame": what he does will match what he writes, so his letters will not seem a mere attempt to frighten. Or Paul may leave unspoken "I say this", as in 1 Corinthians 7:6. The sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: boast
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Balanced and Readable often speak of pride, but in chapters 10-12 Paul's argument turns on the word "boast" itself, ironically used, so every level keeps it, as in 1 Corinthians 1:29-31 (the settled choice on boasting).

decisions.choice: The Lord gave us this authority to build you up, not to knock you down.
alternatives: which the Lord gave for building up and not for tearing down
decisions.reason: Readable makes the relative clause a sentence of its own, naming the Lord again. "Knock down" repeats the verb of verse 4 at this level.

decisions.choice: se vanter at every level, with "la vantardise" and "le sujet de fierté" for the nouns (for chapters 10-11, as in 12-13)
decisions.reason: In chapters 10-12 Paul's argument turns on the word itself, used with irony, so every level keeps "se vanter" (docs/corinthians-terms.md), where chapters 7-9 say "être fier" at Balanced and Readable. "Vantardise" suits the fool's speech Paul is about to make; "sujet de fierté" is used where his boast is a good one (11:10).

decisions.choice: gloriarse at every level (chapters 10-12)
alternatives: sentirse orgulloso (B, R) as in chapters 1-9
decisions.reason: In chapters 1-9 Balanced and Readable say "orgullo" for proper pride. In chapters 10-12 Paul's argument turns on the boasting word itself, as he takes up his rivals' boasting with irony, so the same word must be heard each time; Spanish keeps "gloriarse" at every level, as 1 Corinthians 1:31 does and as the English keeps "boast". "Jactarse" always sounds like bragging and would make Paul's boasting in the Lord sound wrong.

decisions.choice: kujivunia at every level (chapters 10-12)
decisions.reason: Recorded for chapters 10-12. Here Paul begins the boasting his rivals have forced on him (meaning decision), and his ironic boasting carries the argument, so Balanced and Readable keep the boasting verb "kujivunia" (and "kujivuna" without an object), as the English keeps "boast" at all three levels; "kuona fahari" (1:12) would lose the irony. "Kujisifu" is kept for recommending oneself (3:1; 10:12) and "kujigamba" for bragging.

decisions.choice: "quyền" for exousia
decisions.reason: The right and power of an apostle (m2); the word the Vietnamese 1 Corinthians 9 uses for Paul's rights, and the same in 13:10.

decisions.choice: "gây dựng ... phá đổ" (L, B); "gây dựng ... đánh đổ" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of Jeremiah's call (m3); "gây dựng" is the book's word for oikodome, and "phá đổ" picks up the same noun from 10:4.

decisions.choice: "자랑하다" at every level, through chapters 10-12
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as the boasting Paul's rivals force on him; it is not the good pride of 7:4, so Readable keeps the plain "자랑하다" here and in all of chapters 10-12.

decisions.choice: "권위" at every level; "세우다", "무너뜨리다" (L, B); "세우다", "쓰러뜨리다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as an apostle's authority, given by the Lord; "권리" is kept for the right of 1 Corinthians 9.

decisions.choice: "[이렇게 말합니다]" (L)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the purpose clause has no main verb close at hand.

source.text: ὅτι Αἱ ἐπιστολαὶ μέν, φησίν, βαρεῖαι καὶ ἰσχυραί, ἡ δὲ παρουσία τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενὴς καὶ ὁ λόγος ἐξουθενημένος.

records.literal_gloss: Because the letters indeed, he says, [are] weighty and strong, but the presence of the body weak and the speech having been despised.

en.L: For "[His] letters," he says, "[are] weighty and strong, but the presence of [his] body [is] weak and [his] speech despised."
en.B: For someone says, "His letters are weighty and strong, but when he is here in person he is weak, and the way he speaks is contemptible."
en.R: Someone there says, "His letters are strong and hard-hitting. But when he is with us in person, he is weak, and his speaking is not worth listening to."

fr.L: Car « [ses] lettres, dit-il, [sont] lourdes et fortes, mais la présence de [son] corps [est] faible et [sa] parole méprisée ».
fr.B: Quelqu’un dit en effet : « Ses lettres ont du poids et de la force, mais quand il est là en personne, il est faible, et sa façon de parler est méprisable. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un là-bas dit : « Ses lettres sont fortes et frappent dur. Mais quand il est avec nous en personne, il est faible, et ce qu’il dit ne vaut pas la peine d’être écouté. »

es.L: Porque «[sus] cartas», dice, «[son] severas y fuertes, pero la presencia del cuerpo [es] débil y la palabra, despreciable».
es.B: Porque alguien dice: «Sus cartas son severas y fuertes, pero cuando está aquí en persona es débil, y su manera de hablar es despreciable».
es.R: Alguien de allí dice: «Sus cartas son fuertes y duras. Pero cuando está con nosotros en persona, es débil, y no vale la pena escucharlo».

sw.L: Kwa maana, "Barua [zake]," anasema, "[ni] nzito na zenye nguvu, lakini uwepo wa mwili [wake] ni dhaifu, na usemi [wake] umedharauliwa."
sw.B: Kwa maana mtu mmoja anasema, "Barua zake ni nzito na zenye nguvu, lakini akiwa hapa ana kwa ana ni dhaifu, na jinsi anavyozungumza ni ya kudharauliwa."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja huko anasema, "Barua zake ni kali na zenye nguvu. Lakini anapokuwa nasi ana kwa ana, ni dhaifu, na maneno yake hayafai kusikilizwa."

vi.L: Vì người ta nói: "Các thư của ông ấy thì nặng nề và mạnh mẽ, nhưng sự hiện diện bằng thân thể thì yếu đuối, và lời nói thì đáng khinh."
vi.B: Vì có người nói: "Thư của ông ấy thì nặng nề và mạnh mẽ, nhưng khi có mặt ở đây thì ông ấy yếu đuối, và cách ông ấy nói thì đáng khinh."
vi.R: Có người ở đó nói: "Thư của ông ấy thì mạnh mẽ và gay gắt. Nhưng khi ở với chúng ta thì ông ấy yếu đuối, và lời ông ấy nói chẳng đáng nghe."

ko.L: "[그의] 편지는 무게가 있고 힘이 있지만, 몸으로 와 있을 때에는 약하고, [그의] 말은 보잘것없다" 하고 그가 말합니다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람은 이렇게 말합니다. "그의 편지는 무게가 있고 강하지만, 직접 와 있을 때에는 약하고, 그가 말하는 것은 들을 가치도 없다."
ko.R: 그곳의 어떤 사람은 이렇게 말합니다. "그의 편지는 강하고 날카롭다. 그러나 그가 우리와 함께 있을 때에는 약하고, 그의 말은 들을 가치가 없다."

decisions.choice: the words after "for" quote what a critic says about Paul
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts have no quotation marks, but φησίν ("he says") marks the words around it as speech, and the SBLGNT begins them with a capital letter. The quotation runs to the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: he says: a particular critic, or "someone says"
decisions.reason: φησίν is singular. It may point to one leading critic, whom verse 11 calls "such a person", or it may be used loosely for what is being said. The opponents in chapters 10-12 are spoken of both as "some" (verses 2, 12) and as "anyone" (verse 7; 11:4).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "he says" (singular)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the plural, "they say", which differs by one letter and matches the plurals of verses 2 and 12. The SBLGNT reads the singular, found in most manuscripts. The meaning is close either way. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: weighty and strong letters; feeble presence in person; speaking held in contempt
decisions.reason: βαρεῖαι means heavy, so weighty, impressive or severe; ἰσχυραί means strong, forceful. παρουσία τοῦ σώματος is Paul's presence in person, and ἐξουθενημένος means despised, treated as nothing. In Corinth eloquent speech and an impressive bearing were admired; Paul admits he was untrained in speech (11:6) and had not come with fine words (1 Corinthians 2:1-4).

decisions.choice: when he is here in person (B); when he is with us in person (R)
decisions.reason: "Presence of the body" means how he comes across in person (m4); Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: someone says (B); Someone there says (R)
decisions.reason: "Someone" leaves open whether one critic is meant (m2). Readable puts the speaker first, as English usually does.

decisions.choice: "người ta nói" (L); "có người nói" (B); "Có người ở đó nói" (R) for phesin
decisions.reason: A particular critic, or "someone says" (m2, uncertain); Vietnamese needs no pronoun, and "người ta" and "có người" leave the speaker unnamed, as Paul does.

decisions.choice: the critic's words in quotation marks, with "ông ấy" for Paul
decisions.reason: The words quote what a critic says (m1); "ông ấy" is how a Vietnamese critic would speak of a man he does not respect.

decisions.choice: The critic's words in the plain style ("보잘것없다")
decisions.reason: A quoted slogan is in 해라체, as in 1 Corinthians.

decisions.choice: "그가 말합니다" (L); "어떤 사람은 ... 말합니다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Follows the SBLGNT singular, read by the meaning decision as one critic or "someone".

source.text: τοῦτο λογιζέσθω ὁ τοιοῦτος, ὅτι οἷοί ἐσμεν τῷ λόγῳ δι’ ἐπιστολῶν ἀπόντες, τοιοῦτοι καὶ παρόντες τῷ ἔργῳ.

records.literal_gloss: This let reckon such a one, that such as we are in word through letters being absent, such also being present in deed.

en.L: Let such a person reckon this: that what we are in word through letters when absent, such [we are] also in deed when present.
en.B: Anyone who says this should understand that we are the same in action when we are with you as we are in the words of our letters when we are away.
en.R: People who talk like that should know this: when we come, what we do will be just as strong as what we write in our letters when we are away.

fr.L: Que celui-là considère ceci : tels nous sommes en parole par lettres quand nous sommes absents, tels [nous sommes] aussi en acte quand nous sommes présents.
fr.B: Celui qui dit cela doit comprendre que nous sommes les mêmes dans nos actes quand nous sommes avec vous que dans les paroles de nos lettres quand nous sommes loin.
fr.R: Les gens qui parlent ainsi doivent savoir ceci : quand nous viendrons, ce que nous ferons sera aussi fort que ce que nous écrivons dans nos lettres quand nous sommes loin.

es.L: Que tal persona considere esto: que tales como somos en palabra por medio de cartas, estando ausentes, tales [somos] también en hechos, estando presentes.
es.B: Quien dice esto debe entender que, cuando estamos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, somos en los hechos lo mismo que somos en las palabras de nuestras cartas cuando estamos lejos.
es.R: Los que hablan así deben saber esto: cuando lleguemos, lo que hagamos será tan fuerte como lo que escribimos en nuestras cartas cuando estamos lejos.

sw.L: Mtu wa aina hiyo alizingatie hili: kwamba kile tulicho kwa neno kupitia barua tukiwa mbali, ndicho [tulicho] pia kwa tendo tukiwapo.
sw.B: Yeyote anayesema hivyo aelewe kwamba tutakapokuwa pamoja nanyi, matendo yetu yatakuwa sawa kabisa na maneno ya barua zetu tunapokuwa mbali.
sw.R: Watu wanaosema hivyo wajue hili: tutakapokuja, tutakachotenda kitakuwa na nguvu sawa na tunachoandika katika barua zetu tukiwa mbali.

vi.L: Người như thế hãy tính điều này: chúng tôi qua các thư khi vắng mặt thể nào trong lời nói, thì khi có mặt cũng thể ấy trong việc làm.
vi.B: Ai nói như vậy nên hiểu rằng khi có mặt với anh chị em, chúng tôi hành động đúng như những lời chúng tôi viết trong thư khi vắng mặt.
vi.R: Những người nói như vậy nên biết điều này: khi chúng tôi đến, những gì chúng tôi làm sẽ mạnh mẽ đúng như những gì chúng tôi viết trong thư khi ở xa.

ko.L: 그런 사람은 이것을 여겨야 합니다. 우리가 떠나 있을 때 편지로 하는 말이 어떠하든지, 함께 있을 때 행동으로도 그와 같다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그런 말을 하는 사람은 알아야 합니다. 우리가 멀리 있을 때 편지로 하는 말과 같이, 여러분과 함께 있을 때 우리가 하는 행동도 그와 같습니다.
ko.R: 그렇게 말하는 사람들은 이것을 알아야 합니다. 우리가 가면, 우리가 하는 일은 우리가 멀리 있을 때 편지에 쓰는 말만큼 강할 것입니다.

decisions.choice: such a person: whoever says what verse 10 quotes
decisions.reason: ὁ τοιοῦτος points back to the speaker of verse 10, without naming him. λογιζέσθω ("let him reckon") is the verb of verses 2 and 7 again: let the critics count on this.

decisions.choice: Paul is the same in word and in deed, and his next visit will show it
decisions.reason: οἷοί ... τοιοῦτοι ("such as ... such") sets the two halves side by side; the verb of the second half is understood. The present tense states what Paul always is, but the point is the visit to come (12:20-13:2, 10).

decisions.choice: when we come, what we do will be just as strong
alternatives: such we are also in deed when present
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sentence means for the coming visit (m2).

decisions.choice: "người như thế" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is already man or woman.

decisions.choice: "여겨야 합니다" (L); "알아야 합니다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb of verses 2 and 7 again, kept in Literal.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ τολμῶμεν ἐγκρῖναι ἢ συγκρῖναι ἑαυτούς τισιν τῶν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστανόντων· ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἑαυτοὺς μετροῦντες καὶ συγκρίνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς οὐ συνιᾶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Not for we dare to class or to compare ourselves with some of the [ones] themselves commending; but they, by themselves themselves measuring and comparing themselves with themselves, not do understand.

en.L: For we do not dare to class or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves; but they, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, do not understand.
en.B: We would not dare to put ourselves in the same class as some of those who recommend themselves, or to set ourselves beside them. They use themselves as the measuring stick and compare themselves with themselves, and that shows how little they understand.
en.R: We would never dare to put ourselves in the same group as those people who recommend themselves, or even to compare ourselves with them. They make up their own standards, and then they measure themselves by those standards. They compare themselves with each other. They do not understand anything!

fr.L: Car nous n’osons pas nous classer ni nous comparer avec certains de ceux qui se recommandent eux-mêmes ; mais eux, se mesurant eux-mêmes à eux-mêmes et se comparant eux-mêmes à eux-mêmes, ne comprennent pas.
fr.B: Nous n’oserions pas nous mettre dans la même catégorie que certains de ceux qui se recommandent eux-mêmes, ni nous placer à côté d’eux. Ils se prennent eux-mêmes comme mesure et se comparent à eux-mêmes, et cela montre bien leur manque d’intelligence.
fr.R: Nous n’oserions jamais nous mettre dans le même groupe que ces gens qui se recommandent eux-mêmes, ni même nous comparer à eux. Ils inventent leurs propres règles, puis ils se mesurent d’après ces règles. Ils se comparent les uns aux autres. Ils ne comprennent rien !

es.L: Porque no nos atrevemos a incluirnos o compararnos con algunos de los que se recomiendan a sí mismos; pero ellos, midiéndose a sí mismos por sí mismos y comparándose consigo mismos, no entienden.
es.B: No nos atreveríamos a ponernos en la misma categoría que algunos de esos que se recomiendan a sí mismos, ni a compararnos con ellos. Ellos se usan a sí mismos como vara de medir y se comparan consigo mismos, y eso muestra lo poco que entienden.
es.R: Nunca nos atreveríamos a ponernos en el mismo grupo que esas personas que se recomiendan a sí mismas, ni siquiera a compararnos con ellas. Ellas inventan sus propias reglas, y luego se miden con esas reglas. Se comparan unas con otras. ¡No entienden nada!

sw.L: Kwa maana hatuthubutu kujiweka katika kundi moja na, au kujilinganisha na, baadhi ya wale wanaojitambulisha wenyewe; lakini wao, wakijipima wenyewe kwa wenyewe na kujilinganisha wenyewe na wenyewe, hawaelewi.
sw.B: Hatungethubutu kujiweka katika kundi moja na baadhi ya wale wanaojitambulisha wenyewe, wala kujilinganisha nao. Wao hujifanya kipimo chao wenyewe na kujilinganisha na wao wenyewe, na hilo linaonyesha jinsi wasivyoelewa.
sw.R: Kamwe hatungethubutu kujiweka katika kundi la watu wale wanaojisifu wenyewe, wala hata kujilinganisha nao. Wao hujitungia vipimo vyao wenyewe, kisha wanajipima kwa vipimo hivyo. Wanajilinganisha wao kwa wao. Hawaelewi chochote!

vi.L: Vì chúng tôi không dám xếp mình vào hàng hoặc so sánh mình với một số người tự giới thiệu mình; nhưng họ, tự đo mình bằng chính mình và tự so sánh mình với chính mình, thì chẳng hiểu biết gì.
vi.B: Chúng tôi không dám xếp mình vào cùng hàng với một số người tự giới thiệu mình, hoặc đặt mình bên cạnh họ. Họ lấy chính mình làm thước đo và tự so sánh mình với chính mình, và điều đó cho thấy họ hiểu biết ít ỏi biết bao.
vi.R: Chúng tôi chẳng bao giờ dám xếp mình vào cùng nhóm với những người tự giới thiệu mình ấy, hay dù chỉ so sánh mình với họ. Họ tự đặt ra tiêu chuẩn riêng, rồi tự đo mình bằng những tiêu chuẩn đó. Họ so sánh mình với nhau. Họ chẳng hiểu gì cả!

ko.L: 우리는 자기 자신을 추천하는 어떤 사람들과 감히 우리 자신을 같은 부류에 넣거나 비교하지 않습니다. 그러나 그들은 자기들끼리 자기들을 재고, 자기들끼리 자기들을 비교하니, 깨닫지 못합니다.
ko.B: 우리는 자기 자신을 추천하는 어떤 사람들과 감히 같은 부류에 들거나 그들과 나란히 서려고 하지 않습니다. 그들은 자기 자신을 잣대로 삼고 자기들끼리 비교합니다. 그것은 그들이 얼마나 깨닫지 못하는지 보여 줍니다.
ko.R: 우리는 자기 자신을 추천하는 그 사람들과 같은 무리에 들거나 그들과 우리를 비교할 엄두도 내지 않습니다. 그들은 자기들 마음대로 기준을 만들고, 그 기준으로 자기들을 잽니다. 그들은 서로 자기들을 비교합니다. 그들은 아무것도 모릅니다!

decisions.choice: we do not dare: ironic; Paul will not stoop to the rivals' kind of comparison
decisions.reason: τολμῶμεν ("we dare") picks up the daring of verse 2, and Paul says it with irony: these people are so impressive that he would not dare join their ranks. ἐγκρῖναι and συγκρῖναι sound alike, "to class with" and "to compare with", a play on words.

decisions.choice: those who recommend themselves
decisions.reason: συνιστανόντων is the verb of 3:1; 4:2; 5:12, used for introducing and vouching for someone, as letters of recommendation did. The rivals recommend themselves; verse 18 says whose recommendation counts.

decisions.choice: they measure themselves by their own standard
alternatives: they measure themselves by one another, within their own group
decisions.reason: ἑαυτοῖς ἑαυτοὺς can mean each measures himself by himself, or they measure themselves among themselves. Either way there is no standard outside themselves, and no measure from God, which is what verses 13-16 go on to speak of.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "they do not understand", with "but we" at the start of verse 13
alternatives: the words are lacking, so that the measuring by oneself in verse 12 describes Paul
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, mostly Greek-Latin ones, lack οὐ συνιᾶσιν and the opening words of verse 13, which turns the sentence around: Paul and his companions measure themselves by themselves and do not boast beyond measure. The SBLGNT follows the longer text, found in most manuscripts, including early ones. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: recommend
decisions.reason: As in 3:1 and 5:12, Balanced says "recommend", which keeps the link with letters of recommendation (m2); Readable does the same here so that verse 18 can repeat it. Literal says "commend".

decisions.choice: put ourselves in the same class as ... set ourselves beside them
decisions.reason: Balanced gives each of the two similar verbs its own phrase (m1).

decisions.choice: They make up their own standards
decisions.reason: Readable says what measuring oneself by oneself means (m3).

decisions.choice: se recommander, recommander (every level), the same in verse 18
decisions.reason: French "recommander" covers both the English Literal "commend" and the Balanced "recommend", and keeps the link with letters of recommendation (3:1), so one verb serves every level.

decisions.choice: recomendarse (every level)
decisions.reason: As in 3:1 and 5:12, "recomendar" is presenting someone as trustworthy. In chapters 10-12 the word comes back in 10:18 and 12:11, where the Lord and the Corinthians are the ones who should recommend, so Readable keeps "recomendar" too, as the English does.

decisions.choice: wanaojitambulisha (L, B); wanaojisifu (R)
decisions.reason: As set in 3:1: "kujitambulisha" (to present oneself as trustworthy) at Literal and Balanced, "kujisifu" (to praise oneself) at Readable. "Kujipendekeza" would mean currying favor.

decisions.choice: "tự giới thiệu mình" for synistemi with the reflexive
decisions.reason: The book's word for synistemi (3:1; 5:12): those who recommend themselves (m2).

decisions.choice: "không dám" (L, B); "chẳng bao giờ dám" (R)
decisions.reason: The words are ironic (m1); "dám" keeps the irony, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "추천하다" at every level, as at 3:1 and 5:12
decisions.reason: The verb the project uses for commending in this letter.

decisions.choice: "감히" (L, B); "엄두도 내지 않다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as ironic; Korean "감히" carries the irony.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχησόμεθα, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τοῦ κανόνος οὗ ἐμέρισεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεὸς μέτρου, ἐφικέσθαι ἄχρι καὶ ὑμῶν οὐ γὰρ ὡς μὴ ἐφικνούμενοι εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπερεκτείνομεν ἑαυτούς, ἄχρι γὰρ καὶ ὑμῶν ἐφθάσαμεν ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχώμενοι ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις κόποις, ἐλπίδα δὲ ἔχοντες αὐξανομένης τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν μεγαλυνθῆναι κατὰ τὸν κανόνα ἡμῶν εἰς περισσείαν, εἰς τὰ ὑπερέκεινα ὑμῶν εὐαγγελίσασθαι, οὐκ ἐν ἀλλοτρίῳ κανόνι εἰς τὰ ἕτοιμα καυχήσασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: We but not into the [things] beyond measure will boast, but according to the measure of the sphere which apportioned to us the God, of a measure, to reach as far as even you. \v 14 Not for as not reaching to you are we overextending ourselves, as far as for even you we came in the gospel of the Christ, \v 15 not into the [things] beyond measure boasting in others' labors, hope but having, increasing the faith of you, among you to be enlarged according to the sphere of us into abundance, \v 16 into the [places] beyond you to proclaim the gospel, not in another's sphere into the [things] ready to boast.

en.L: But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the sphere which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even as far as you. \v 14 For we are not overextending ourselves, as [though we] did not reach to you, for we came even as far as you in the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 15 not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, but having hope that, as your faith grows, we will be enlarged among you according to our sphere, to overflowing, \v 16 so as to proclaim the gospel in the [lands] beyond you, not to boast in another's sphere of things [already] made ready.
en.B: But we will not boast of things outside our measure. We will boast only within the measure of the field that God has measured out to us as ours, and it reaches even as far as you. \v 14 We are not overstretching ourselves, as we would be if our field did not reach you; we did reach you, bringing the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 15 We do not boast of things outside our measure, in work that others have done. We hope instead that as your faith grows, we will be given far more room among you, still within our field, \v 16 so that we can carry the gospel to the lands beyond you, without boasting of ground someone else has already prepared.
en.R: But we will not boast about things outside the limits God set for us. We will boast only about the work in the area God gave us, and that area reaches all the way to you. \v 14 We are not stretching the truth when we boast about you. We really did come all the way to you; we were the first to bring you the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 15 We do not boast about work that other people have done. We hope that your faith will keep growing. Then our work among you can become much bigger, but still in the area God gave us. \v 16 Then we can tell the good news in places far beyond you. We do not want to boast about what someone else has already done in their own area.

fr.L: Mais nous, nous ne nous vanterons pas au-delà de la mesure, mais selon la mesure du domaine que Dieu nous a attribué comme mesure, [pour] parvenir même jusqu’à vous. \v 14 Car nous ne nous étendons pas trop loin, comme si nous ne parvenions pas jusqu’à vous, car nous sommes arrivés même jusqu’à vous avec l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 15 ne nous vantant pas au-delà de la mesure dans les travaux d’autrui, mais ayant l’espérance que, votre foi grandissant, nous serons agrandis parmi vous selon notre domaine, jusqu’à déborder, \v 16 pour annoncer l’Évangile dans les [régions] au-delà de chez vous, sans nous vanter dans le domaine d’autrui de choses [déjà] toutes prêtes.
fr.B: Mais nous, nous ne nous vanterons pas de ce qui dépasse notre mesure. Nous nous vanterons seulement dans la mesure du champ d’action que Dieu nous a attribué comme le nôtre, et il s’étend jusqu’à vous. \v 14 Nous ne nous étendons pas trop loin, comme ce serait le cas si notre champ d’action ne vous atteignait pas ; nous sommes bien arrivés jusqu’à vous, en apportant l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 15 Nous ne nous vantons pas de ce qui dépasse notre mesure, du travail que d’autres ont fait. Nous espérons au contraire que, votre foi grandissant, nous recevrons parmi vous beaucoup plus d’espace, toujours dans notre champ d’action, \v 16 pour que nous puissions porter l’Évangile dans les pays situés au-delà de chez vous, sans nous vanter d’un terrain que quelqu’un d’autre a déjà préparé.
fr.R: Mais nous ne nous vanterons pas de choses qui dépassent les limites que Dieu nous a fixées. Nous nous vanterons seulement du travail fait dans le secteur que Dieu nous a donné, et ce secteur va jusqu’à vous. \v 14 Nous n’exagérons pas quand nous nous vantons à votre sujet. Nous sommes vraiment venus jusqu’à vous ; nous avons été les premiers à vous apporter la bonne nouvelle au sujet du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. \v 15 Nous ne nous vantons pas du travail que d’autres ont fait. Nous espérons que votre foi va continuer à grandir. Alors notre travail parmi vous pourra devenir beaucoup plus grand, mais toujours dans le secteur que Dieu nous a donné. \v 16 Ensuite, nous pourrons annoncer la bonne nouvelle dans des endroits bien au-delà de chez vous. Nous ne voulons pas nous vanter de ce que quelqu’un d’autre a déjà fait dans son propre secteur.

es.L: Pero nosotros no nos gloriaremos sin medida, sino conforme a la medida de la esfera que Dios nos asignó como medida, para llegar también hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 14 Porque no nos estamos extralimitando, como si no hubiéramos llegado hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pues llegamos también hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con el evangelio del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}; \v 15 no gloriándonos sin medida en trabajos ajenos, sino teniendo esperanza de que, a medida que crezca {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe, seremos engrandecidos entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} conforme a nuestra esfera, hasta rebosar, \v 16 para anunciar el evangelio en los [lugares] más allá de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no para gloriarnos en la esfera de otro de cosas [ya] preparadas.
es.B: Pero nosotros no nos gloriaremos de cosas que están fuera de nuestra medida. Nos gloriaremos solo dentro de la medida del campo que Dios nos ha asignado como nuestro, y ese campo llega hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 14 No nos estamos extralimitando, como sería el caso si nuestro campo no llegara hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; nosotros sí llegamos hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, llevando el evangelio {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. \v 15 No nos gloriamos de cosas fuera de nuestra medida, en trabajos que otros han hecho. Al contrario, esperamos que, a medida que crezca {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe, se nos abra mucho más espacio entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, siempre dentro de nuestro campo, \v 16 para que podamos llevar el evangelio a las tierras que están más allá de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sin gloriarnos de un terreno que otro ya ha preparado.
es.R: Pero no nos gloriaremos de cosas que están fuera de los límites que Dios nos puso. Solo nos gloriaremos del trabajo en el área que Dios nos dio, y esa área llega hasta donde {{plural_you:están ustedes|estáis vosotros}}. \v 14 No exageramos cuando nos gloriamos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. De verdad llegamos hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; fuimos los primeros en {{plural_you:llevarles|llevaros}} la buena noticia acerca {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. \v 15 No nos gloriamos del trabajo que otras personas han hecho. Esperamos que la fe de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} siga creciendo. Entonces nuestro trabajo entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} podrá hacerse mucho más grande, pero siempre en el área que Dios nos dio. \v 16 Así podremos anunciar la buena noticia en lugares mucho más allá de donde {{plural_you:están ustedes|estáis vosotros}}. No queremos gloriarnos de lo que otro ya ha hecho en su propia área.

sw.L: Lakini sisi hatutajivunia kupita kipimo, bali kwa kadiri ya kipimo cha fungu ambalo Mungu ametugawia kuwa kipimo, kufika hata kwenu. \v 14 Kwa maana hatujinyooshi kupita kiasi, kana kwamba hatukufika kwenu, kwa maana tulifika hata kwenu katika Injili ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 15 bila kujivunia kupita kipimo katika kazi za wengine, lakini tukiwa na tumaini kwamba, imani yenu ikikua, tutakuzwa kati yenu kwa kadiri ya fungu letu, hata kufurika, \v 16 ili kuhubiri habari njema katika [nchi] zilizo mbali zaidi yenu, si kujivunia katika fungu la mwingine mambo [yaliyokwisha] kuwa tayari.
sw.B: Lakini sisi hatutajivunia mambo yaliyo nje ya kipimo chetu. Tutajivunia tu ndani ya kipimo cha uwanja ambao Mungu ametupimia kuwa wetu, nao unafika hata kwenu. \v 14 Hatujinyooshi kupita kiasi, kama tungefanya ikiwa uwanja wetu haukufika kwenu; kwa kweli tulifika kwenu tukiwaletea Injili ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 15 Hatujivunii mambo yaliyo nje ya kipimo chetu, yaani kazi waliyoifanya wengine.
